findings.description: CompareNewspaceLabels compares only the levels of the two labels, not (level, weight, char orbit). The body is `s eq t select 0 else (SplitNewspaceLabel(s) lt SplitNewspaceLabel(t) select -1 else 1)`, but SplitNewspaceLabel returns THREE separate values (not a sequence, unlike SplitNewformLabel), and in a Magma expression context only the first return value is used. So the comparison reduces to N(s) lt N(t). For two distinct labels with the same level, N lt N is false, so the intrinsic returns 1 regardless of order: CompareNewspaceLabels("11.2.a","11.4.a") and CompareNewspaceLabels("11.4.a","11.2.a") both return 1, and CompareNewspaceLabels("11.2.a","11.2.b") returns 1. This is not a valid comparison function (violates antisymmetry) and silently gives wrong sort orders. Correct behavior (per the docstring and by analogy with the working CompareNewformLabels) is lexicographic comparison on (N,k,o) returning -1/0/1. CompareNewformLabels does not have this bug because SplitNewformLabel returns a single sequence.
findings.evidence:
cd /home/claude/Magma && magma -b (script t1.m):
CompareNewspaceLabels(11.2.a, 11.4.a) = 1 (expect -1)
CompareNewspaceLabels(11.4.a, 11.2.a) = 1 (expect 1)
CompareNewspaceLabels(11.2.a, 13.2.a) = -1 (expect -1)
CompareNewspaceLabels(11.2.a, 11.2.b) = 1 (expect -1)
Both orderings of ("11.2.a","11.4.a") return 1, so the function is not antisymmetric. Root cause verified: `a,b,c := SplitNewspaceLabel("11.2.a");` yields three values 11 2 1 (three separate return values, only the first of which is used in an expression context).

findings.description: The signature declares four scalar return values (`-> RngIntElt,RngIntElt,RngIntElt,RngIntElt`) and the docstring says 'return the level N, weight k, char orbit, Hecke orbit', but the body returns a SINGLE sequence `[N,k,o,n]`. Multi-assignment as the signature advertises (`N,k,o,n := SplitNewformLabel(s);`) fails at runtime. The sequence return is load-bearing (CompareNewformLabels relies on sequence `lt`), so the right minimal fix is to correct the declared return type and docstring rather than the body. Note the contrast with SplitNewspaceLabel, which genuinely returns three values.
findings.evidence:
Magma transcript (t1.m):
SplitNewformLabel type: SeqEnum value [ 11, 2, 1, 1 ]
multi-assign SplitNewformLabel FAILED: Runtime error in :=: Expected to assign 4 value(s) but only computed 1 value(s)

findings.description: Same defect as SplitNewformLabel, worse count mismatch: the signature declares four scalar return values (`-> RngIntElt,RngIntElt,RngIntElt,RngIntElt`) but the body returns a single sequence of SIX integers [N,k,o,x,n,i] (the docstring correctly lists six quantities, contradicting the declared four return values). Multi-assignment per the signature fails.
findings.evidence:
Magma transcript (t1.m):
SplitEmbedded type: SeqEnum value [ 11, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1 ]
(single SeqEnum of length 6, not four scalar returns)
findings.proposed_fix:
Current line 33:
intrinsic SplitEmbeddedNewformLabel(s::MonStgElt) -> RngIntElt,RngIntElt,RngIntElt,RngIntElt
Replacement:
intrinsic SplitEmbeddedNewformLabel(s::MonStgElt) -> SeqEnum[RngIntElt]
and in the docstring, change 'return the level N, ...' to 'return the sequence [N,k,o,x,n,i] giving the level N, ...'.

findings.description: The require condition contradicts its own error message and the intrinsic's 64-bit contract: `require n lt 2^12: "Hecke oribt index n must be less than 2^11.";`. The code packs n-1 into bits 52+ of what the comment and docstring call a '64-bit Hecke orbit code' (the LMFDB stores hecke_orbit_code in a Postgres bigint, i.e. SIGNED 64-bit). The exact boundary is n le 2^11: HeckeOrbitCode(11,2,1,2^11) = 9218868437260959755 < 2^63, but HeckeOrbitCode(11,2,1,2^11+1) = 9223372036888330251 >= 2^63 = 9223372036854775808, which does not fit in a signed 64-bit integer. So for 2^11 < n < 2^12 the require passes yet the returned code violates the 64-bit claim and would overflow the LMFDB bigint column. The message says 'less than 2^11', the code checks 'less than 2^12'; the mathematically correct bound is n le 2^11. Also 'oribt' is misspelled.
findings.evidence:
Magma transcript:
2^63 = 9223372036854775808
HeckeOrbitCode(11,2,1,2^11) = 9218868437260959755 (lt 2^63: true)
HeckeOrbitCode(11,2,1,2^11+1) = 9223372036888330251 (lt 2^63: false)
HeckeOrbitCode(11,2,1,2^11+5) = 9241386435397812235, ge 2^63: true
All accepted without error by the current require. Oracle for the encoding itself: LMFDB SQL 'SELECT label,hecke_orbit_code FROM mf_newforms WHERE label IN (...)' gives 11.2.a.a -> 33554443, 23.1.b.a -> 68736253975, 7.3.b.a -> 68769808391, 100.6.a.d -> 13510798982774884, 983.2.c.a -> 137472508887, all matching HeckeOrbitCode(N,k,o,n) exactly, confirming the packing layout and that bits 52-62 (11 usable bits for n-1 under signed 64) are the intended budget.

findings.description: Docstring says 'Compares newform label strings of the form N.k.a.x' (copy-paste from CompareNewformLabels), but the intrinsic actually requires embedded newform labels of the form N.k.a.x.n.i and raises a runtime error on the documented N.k.a.x form (SplitEmbeddedNewformLabel indexes r[5], r[6]). The docstring should describe the 6-component form and the additional Conrey index / embedding index comparison keys.

Magma transcript:
try x := CompareEmbeddedNewformLabels("11.2.a.a","11.2.a.b"); catch -> N.k.a.x form ERRORS: Runtime error in '[]': Sequence index 5 should be in the range 1 to 4
Works correctly on true embedded labels: CompareEmbeddedNewformLabels("11.2.a.a.1.1","11.2.a.a.1.2") = -1.

findings.description: The first require message in HeckeOrbitCode names the wrong intrinsic: 'Inputs to NewformLabel must be positive integers.' (copy-paste from NewformLabel). A user violating the positivity requirement of HeckeOrbitCode is told about NewformLabel.

coverage_notes: All 15 intrinsics in mfutils.m (lines 1-128) were both read and executed. Tested with independent oracles: AnalyticConductor (5 values vs LMFDB mf_newforms.analytic_conductor, agree to double precision, hardcoded in tests); HeckeOrbitCode (5 values vs LMFDB mf_newforms.hecke_orbit_code, exact match, hardcoded; plus roundtrip with SplitHeckeOrbitCode including max-field values and signed-64-bit boundary probing at n=2^11 and 2^11+1); anlist_from_aplist (vs Magma built-in q-expansions in 4 configurations: 11.2.a.a via EllipticCurve 11a1, 20a1 exercising the p|N branch with a_p both 0 and nonzero, newform 7.3.b.a with nontrivial odd quadratic character, and Delta 1.12.a.a; plus m=1 edge case; recurrence a_{p^{r+1}} = a_p a_{p^r} - chi(p) p^{k-1} a_{p^{r-1}} verified correct); NewformLabel/NewspaceLabel/Gamma1Label + Split* (roundtrips over parameter grids including multi-letter base-26 codes, plus LMFDB label spot checks, plus the string-Conrey-label and GrpDrchElt variants); Compare* (equality, numeric-vs-string ordering, each component position). Not tested: m=0 in anlist_from_aplist (errors on an[1]:=1 — undocumented but arguably out-of-domain, not reported); ap sequences with non-integer universes (e.g. cyclotomic ap) in anlist_from_aplist were only reasoned about, not executed — the code is universe-generic and nothing looked suspicious; NewformLabel(chi::GrpDrchElt,...) variant does not exist (only MonStgElt), noted but not filed since it is an omission, not a bug. Degenerate/duplicate-parse label comparisons (e.g. "011.2.a" vs "11.2.a" returning 1 instead of 0) were noted but not filed as they require malformed input.
